name: Lentiviral vector (HIV-1-derived)
short_description: HIV-1 rebuilt as a gene-delivery shuttle — almost the entire viral genome removed, the packaging genes split across separate producer-cell plasmids, leaving a VSV-G-pseudotyped envelope and the conical Gag capsid to deliver a therapeutic cargo gene (flanked by self-inactivating LTRs) that reverse transcriptase and integrase write into the target cell's genome. Replication-incompetent: it cannot make more of itself.

No labels per house rule (sem gets none). reference: PASS - CDC PHIL #10860 (public domain, CDC/Dr. A. Harrison, Dr. P. Feorino, 1989): colorized TEM of 2-3 clearly resolved, isolated mature HIV-1 virions (magenta envelope, dense dark core) against a uniform green background; normalised 1080x1080 crop has no baked-in text, caption, scale bar or border. This is an HIV-1 plate, NOT a lentiviral-vector-specific image — no freely-licensed vector-specific micrograph could be found (Wikimedia Commons, CDC PHIL, NIAID/NIH Flickr and general web search all checked; the one vector-specific TEM figure found, in Molecular Therapy, is CC BY-NC-ND and was excluded on licence grounds). Disclosed explicitly in the caption per the chlamydia-felis precedent. Free/mature (non-budding) particles were chosen deliberately over a budding-from-cell scene as the more honest visual analogue for a purified, manufactured vector product.
